import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_4.csv"

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)

# Step 2: Analyze join keys and plan joins
# Source2 contains the target column 'Profit' and keys: Ord_id, Prod_id, Ship_id, Cust_id
# Other sources provide dimension info:
# - df0: Prod_id (product info)
# - df1: Ship_id (shipping info)
# - df3: Ord_id (order info)
# - df4: Cust_id (customer info)

# We need to join all sources on their shared keys to get a complete dataset.
# The target only requires the 'Profit' column, so after joining, we select 'Profit'.

# Step 3: Perform joins step-by-step

# Join df2 with df0 on 'Prod_id'
df_20 = pd.merge(df2, df0, how='inner', left_on='Prod_id', right_on='Prod_id')

# Join df_20 with df1 on 'Ship_id'
df_201 = pd.merge(df_20, df1, how='inner', left_on='Ship_id', right_on='Ship_id')

# Join df_201 with df3 on 'Ord_id' (note df3 has 'Ord_id' and 'Order_ID', df2 has 'Ord_id')
df_2013 = pd.merge(df_201, df3, how='inner', left_on='Ord_id', right_on='Ord_id')

# Join df_2013 with df4 on 'Cust_id'
df_final = pd.merge(df_2013, df4, how='inner', left_on='Cust_id', right_on='Cust_id')

# Step 4: Extract the target column 'Profit' only
target_df = df_final[['Profit']].copy()

# Step 5: Ensure 'Profit' is float type as per target schema
target_df['Profit'] = target_df['Profit'].astype(float)

# Step 6: Save the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=True)  # keep index as in examples (e.g., 16,1,9)

# The output CSV will have the same index as the joined dataframe, matching the target examples format.

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_88_2 and Source5_88_1 on Ship_id
result = pd.merge(source2, source1, how='inner', left_on='Ship_id', right_on='Ship_id')

# Join with Source5_88_3 on Ord_id
result = pd.merge(result, source3, how='inner', left_on='Ord_id', right_on='Ord_id')

# Join with Source5_88_4 on Cust_id
result = pd.merge(result, source4, how='inner', left_on='Cust_id', right_on='Cust_id')

# Join with Source5_88_0 on Prod_id
result = pd.merge(result, source0, how='inner', left_on='Prod_id', right_on='Prod_id')

# Aggregate sum of Profit (no group by since target has only one column and no keys)
final = pd.DataFrame()
final['Profit'] = [result['Profit'].sum()]

# Write output
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_88/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
